context.body: Spectacle gives way to a quiet encounter and a broadened view of what God is doing.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The LORD questions Elijah, passes by amid wind, earthquake, and fire, speaks in a low sound, and gives new assignments and a preserved remnant.
observations.label: God questions Elijah and speaks after the storm: action

observations.body: Elijah repeats his complaint and receives work, successors, judgment, and correction of his isolation.
observations.label: God questions Elijah and speaks after the storm: response

observations.body: What are you doing here? · not in the wind · low whisper · seven thousand
observations.label: Words in 1 Kings 19:9–18

payload.posture: Read 1 Kings 19:9–18 as land, judges, and kings evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The narrative says the LORD was not in the three forces without denying that the LORD sent them.
payload.title: God questions Elijah and speaks after the storm
